Seminar Title:

The Role of Economic Complexity in Ecological Footprint Mitigation for BRICS Nations: Does Institutional Quality and Globalisation Shape Environmental Sustainability?

Seminar Type:

Progress Seminar

Department:

Humanities and Social Sciences

Speaker Name:

Aksita Pattnaik ( Rollno : 522hs2003)

Speaker Type:

Student

Venue:

MN 437, HS Seminar Room

Date and Time:

29 Jul 2026 04:30 PM

Contact:

Bikash Ranjan Mishra

Abstract:

The rapid economic expansion and industrial transformation of BRICS nations have significantly contributed to global economic growth, but this progress has also intensified environmental pressures, particularly through increased resource consumption, energy demand, and ecological degradation. The study investigates the impact of the economic complexity index, globalisation index, and institutional quality index on the ecological footprint of BRICS nations over the period 2000 to 2022. Taking EF as the dependent variable and ECI, IQ, GDP, URB, REC, GI as the independent variables, the study has utilised the DK estimation method that accounts for cross-sectional dependency and heterogeneity and uses the MMQR method as a means of robustness test. The empirical findings show that ECI has a positive impact on EF in the medium to higher quantiles, signifying that more complex economies tend to consume more resources due to their advanced industries and technologies. Furthermore, GI, even though not significant in lower quantiles, is positive and significant at the higher quantiles. The results imply that countries that already have a large EF base are facing worsening environmental quality due to globalisation. The findings reveal that IQ has a positive and significant effect across all quantiles, which implies that stronger institutions contribute towards EF in the BRICS nations. Stronger institutions often facilitate extensive growth and consumption, leading to overuse of resources and wastage. Moreover, the consumption of renewable energy has shown a consistent adverse impact on the EF across all the quantiles. The findings suggest that adopting cleaner sources of energy will significantly improve the quality of the environment. GDP shows a positive and increasingly significant effect across the higher quantiles, which implies that the wealthy economies pose a higher pressure on the environment. Finally, the findings reveal that URB has a negative and significant impact across the quantiles, suggesting a counterintuitive argument that urban centres are more energy efficient than their rural counterparts.

&nbsp

Keywords: Economic complexity, ecological footprint, BRICS, environmental sustainability.
